shortDescription: The South African rand was steady in early trade on Tuesday ahead of the release of local manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI) and vehicle sales data for August.

children: The South African rand was steady in early trade on Tuesday ahead of the release of local manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI) and vehicle sales data for August.
The rand traded at 16.1008 against the dollar
, little changed from its previous close of 16.1049, as of 0545 GMT.
The August Absa PMI survey, due at 0900 GMT, is expected to provide fresh insight into manufacturing conditions in Africa's most industrialised economy.
South African manufacturing sentiment deteriorated further in July, dragged down by weak export demand and concerns about renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran.

"The PMI is expected to have remained in contractionary territory in August. Both business activity and new sales orders indices were still largely subdued in July. Global uncertainty remains somewhat elevated, while a pick-up in the oil price saw a diesel price hike implemented in August weighing on manufacturers' profitability," Investec economist Lara Hodes said in a note.
Investors will also focus on vehicle sales (ZAVEHY=ECI) data, due at around 1200 GMT, which will offer a snapshot of consumer demand for big-ticket items.
South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) was little changed in early deals, with the yield at 8.63%.
